method: Install the exact Mimo-2.0.pkg over the saved build 4 installation; compare installed helper with the sealed app.

Remove the controller before Rule cleanup; preserve an unrelated PF anchor and enable reference; verify all five jobs, owned PF/DNS/TUN, helper/manager and private IPv6 ownership are removed; bind TCP/UDP listeners after cleanup.
Temporarily remove Mimo.app after cleanup and verify native HTTPS continues.
Inject failure immediately after maintenance and runtime preparation in the bundled installer; verify full inactive rollback, retained settings and native HTTPS even with saved Rule mode.
Run another copy of the pinned mihomo after cleanup and serve real HTTPS through its SOCKS listener; exercise the actual terminal Cancel and Stop-and-Continue paths.
Use real SOCKS TCP, certificate-verified TLS and HTTP responses; inspect those same live connections in the engine to distinguish proxy, exact-domain DIRECT and suffix DIRECT routing.
Query an online native Tailnet peer and require its actual Tailnet IPv4 address after the bypass and mode checks.
Install the final package again, fully deactivate, reboot the VM, verify ports and native HTTPS, then explicitly reactivate Direct before restoring the baseline.
limits: This release is ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized.
VM acceptance does not reproduce the physical fast-user-switch freeze or qualify physical sleep/wake.
Coexistence is verified with another real mihomo; arbitrary third-party VPNs and their installers are not universally qualified.
Installed takeover acceptance uses the real terminal confirmation; native GUI rendering and lifecycle behavior have separate fixture/regression coverage.
Historical engine-only development evidence is not used as proof of full all-daemon deactivation.
